extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A language modeling benchmark dataset constructed from text extracted from Wikipedia articles fitting the Good or Featured article criteria. It is designed to capture longer-term dependencies and features more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora, released in two sizes: WikiText-2 and WikiText-103.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Articles fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia were selected, totaling 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. The raw text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Good and Featured articles extracted from Wikipedia markup via the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Minor bugs such as sort keys and Edit buttons leaking from HTML were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, augmented to further split numbers (8,600 -> 8 @,@ 600) with additional minor fixes. A vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3, and words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Language modeling benchmark to evaluate how sequence models exploit longer contexts, learn long-range dependencies, and handle realistic vocabularies; divided into Train, Valid, and Test partitions.
